correctness.rationale: The moving-hyperplane derivative reduces to two nonnegative differences. For each boundary point the opposite upper cap is paired antipodally; conditional transverse reflection makes each corresponding Euclidean distance larger by the inequality (t+s)^2≥(t−s)^2. Remaining middle-slab weights are nonnegative. Compact approximation and spherical coarea justify quantifiers; exact chord-arc integration proves the complete circle profile; Laplace expansion proves both dimensional coefficients. The standalone numerical checks execute successfully and are explicitly not substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a structural, nontrivial optimality principle for an infinite natural class of weighted geometric cuts, with two different radial measures and all monotone distance weights. It additionally solves the exact affine-offset problem for uniform circle pairs and a two-correction high-dimensional sphere benchmark, providing quantitative models for the recent hyperplane cut objective rather than merely a textbook numerical integral.
